Stress testing 
Along with VaR, stress testing is an important tool used to

the Firm’s vulnerability to losses under a range of stressed

are used to understand the exposures responsible for those 
potential losses and are measured against limits.

**Why gross margin doesn't apply**

Gross margin is defined as `(Revenue − Cost of Goods Sold) / Revenue`. - **Noninterest revenue** — fees, commissions, investment banking, trading, asset management, card income, etc.

The figures below are taken directly from JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s 2022 Form 10-K (the attached `JPMORGAN_2022_10K.pdf`), primarily the "Three-Year Summary of Consolidated Financial Highlights" and the "Executive Overview" of the MD&A.

| Metric (in millions) | 2022 | 2021 | 2020 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total net revenue | $128,695 | $121,649 | $119,951 |
| Net interest income | $66,710 | $52,311 | — |
| Noninterest revenue | $61,985 | $69,338 | — |
| Total noninterest expense | $76,140 | $71,343 | $66,656 |
| Net income | $37,676 | $48,334 | $29,131 |
| Overhead ratio | 59% | 59% | 56% |

The filing reports net yield on interest-earning assets of **2.00%** (FTE) for 2022, up 36 basis points. A full-text search across all 382 pages of the 10-K returned no matches for "gross margin," "gross profit," "cost of goods sold," or "cost of revenue," which is the primary evidence that gross margin is not a metric JPMorgan Chase uses or reports.
